html:
The Nyamal are an Aboriginal Australian people of the eastern Pilbara in Western Australia, in the country around Marble Bar and the upper Shaw and Coongan rivers. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Ngarla and Kariyarra toward the coast, the Palyku to the south and the Nyangumarta to the northeast. Sheep stations spread inland from the 1860s, and gold brought miners to Marble Bar in the 1890s.

On 1 May 1946 Aboriginal workers walked off sheep stations across the Pilbara in the Pilbara strike, led by men including Clancy McKenna and Dooley Bin Bin with the prospector Don McLeod. The strike, among the longest in Australian history, lasted about three years and won better pay and treatment.
